expansion_contract.fact_row: verified official data-schema, coverage, voucher, algorithm or subsidy-control fact
expansion_contract.boundary_row: prevents aggregate coverage, availability percentages, voucher eligibility, future build status or rule-engine outputs from being promoted to exact current postcode or parcel coverage without accepted r2 archive bytes and hardened postjoin evidence

source_routes.name: Ofcom fixed coverage and full-fibre take-up data dictionary v2
BDUK Project Gigabit Voucher Eligibility Engine
BDUK May 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review
Canonical slot state and exact-output acceptance

facts.detail: The January 2026 snapshot was supplied by 52 fixed-network and 18 fixed-wireless-access providers.
Provider submissions cover premises where an end user could order a fixed broadband service on that provider network.
Ofcom uses Ordnance Survey AddressBase Premium and Islands products as the premise base.
The Spring 2026 snapshot uses AddressBase Epoch 123.

guard_streams.write_limit: Provider participation and an address-base record do not prove a specific parcel has accepted current coverage.

facts.detail: The data is published under the Open Government Licence subject to its conditions.
Files are comma-separated values with double-quote text delimiters where applicable.
The data dictionary records a v2 correction dated 7 July 2026.
All 121 all-premises postcode files were renamed from r1 to corrected r2 names.

guard_streams.write_limit: Licence and file naming do not replace byte, member, CRC, hash, schema and row-count acceptance.

facts.detail: Fixed coverage is published at local authority, Westminster constituency, devolved constituency, census output area and postcode levels.
Each detailed geography is supplied for all premises and separately for residential premises.
Output areas use the 2021 census for England, Northern Ireland and Wales and the 2022 census for Scotland.
Postcode files contain both a no-space postcode and a single-space postcode representation.

guard_streams.write_limit: Geographic aggregates and postcode strings require an exact canonical identity join before parcel use.

facts.detail: Gigabit-capable coverage is reported for postcode and census-output-area files.
Full-fibre coverage is not reported at postcode or output-area level because of commercial confidentiality.
Coverage fields refer to fixed-line broadband unless FWA is explicitly named.
Gigabit availability cannot be used to infer confidential postcode-level full-fibre coverage.

guard_streams.write_limit: Do not manufacture postcode full-fibre values from gigabit-capable coverage.

facts.detail: All Premises is the count of premises in scope for the location.
All Matched Premises counts premises matched to at least one provider record with a non-zero predicted download speed.
Unmatched premises are classified as unclassified.
A zero predicted speed does not satisfy the matched-premises definition.

guard_streams.write_limit: Unclassified or unmatched status must remain unknown and must not become a negative parcel-coverage assertion.

facts.detail: SFBB availability means predicted coverage at 30 Mbit/s or greater.
The UFBB 100 field means coverage at 100 Mbit/s or greater.
The UFBB field means coverage at 300 Mbit/s or greater.
Gigabit availability is the percentage of premises covered by a gigabit-capable service.

guard_streams.write_limit: Availability thresholds are maximum service capability classifications, not measured end-user throughput.

facts.detail: Unable-to-receive fields use thresholds X equal to 2, 5, 10 or 30 Mbit/s.
Unable-to-receive percentages use matched premises for the fixed-only threshold measures.
Maximum-download bands are 0–2, 2–5, 5–10, 10–30 and 30–300 Mbit/s.
A separate field represents premises able to receive a maximum download speed of at least 300 Mbit/s.

guard_streams.write_limit: Aggregate speed bands cannot populate a measured speed or exact parcel technology field.

facts.detail: Decent broadband requires at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
The unable-to-receive-decent measure combines fixed broadband, WISP and Mobile FWA evidence.
The combined decent-broadband measure includes non-matched records and zero predicted speeds.
A separate field records premises able to receive decent broadband from a WISP.

guard_streams.write_limit: Combined fixed/FWA eligibility is not proof of installation, order completion or measured service at a parcel.

facts.detail: Next Generation Access covers networks consisting wholly or partly of optical fibre capable of delivering broadband.
Ofcom's analysis includes full fibre, HFC, VDSL and G.Fast connections.
ADSL connections are excluded from the NGA measure.
NGA status is not equivalent to gigabit-capable service.

guard_streams.write_limit: Technology-family classifications must not be collapsed into a single gigabit or full-fibre label.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom data dictionary v2 and Spring 2026 update

facts.detail: Full-fibre take-up uses active broadband lines serving residential or business customers.
One take-up field is the percentage of premises with full-fibre coverage that have an active full-fibre service.
A second take-up field is the percentage of all premises in the local authority with active full-fibre service.
Take-up percentage can fall while active connections rise when coverage expands faster than adoption.

guard_streams.write_limit: Local-authority take-up is contextual and cannot populate postcode coverage or parcel speed.

facts.detail: Eligible homes and businesses may access vouchers worth up to £4,500 toward installation costs.
Existing available download speed must be below 1 Gbit/s.
A gigabit-capable network must be unlikely to be built commercially in the near future.
No government-funded contract may be planned or in place to improve the network.

guard_streams.write_limit: Voucher eligibility is subsidy status, not current broadband availability.

facts.detail: Eligible premises must not be vacant, derelict or built within the previous two years.
A voucher project requires at least two eligible premises; a single connection is not eligible.
Where current speed is below 50 Mbit/s, the new connection must provide at least double the existing speed.
Where current speed is above 50 Mbit/s, the new connection must provide at least 100 Mbit/s.

guard_streams.write_limit: A proposed voucher project and target speed do not prove the network has been built or is live.

facts.detail: Registered suppliers apply for voucher funding on behalf of residents and businesses.
Funding is released only after the network is built and premises are connected.
The beneficiary is asked to confirm that the connection is live and working before payment.
BDUK may inspect equipment, measure and record speeds and assess installation quality during compliance audits.

guard_streams.write_limit: Only retained, premise-specific completion and audit evidence can support a measured or connected status.

facts.detail: The eligibility engine evaluates every UK premise daily.
The production engine uses rule-based SQL checks in Google Cloud.
It produces a per-premise eligibility Go List with true/false output and an ineligibility reason code.
Eligibility unlocks later voucher checks but does not guarantee that a voucher will be awarded.

guard_streams.write_limit: An algorithmic eligibility result must not be treated as network coverage, build completion or current orderability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK algorithmic transparency record and May 2026 OMR

facts.detail: The engine cross-compares Ordnance Survey premise data with BDUK datasets and joins information by UPRN.
Voucher projects undergo additional human checks, and telecommunications organisations can challenge premise eligibility.
BDUK identifies poor data or criteria as an incorrect-eligibility risk and mitigates it through active monitoring.
May 2026 OMR guidance generally maps planned vouchers to White, issued vouchers to Under Review and claimed vouchers to Grey.

guard_streams.write_limit: Voucher status transitions remain subsidy-control classifications and cannot independently promote current parcel coverage.

probe_evidence.method: official Ofcom PDF/HTML and GOV.UK HTML verification plus canonical exact-output readback
